source_refs.note: The seven steps of experimental design and the worked mouse experiment (PDF 204-205). The exercises (PDF 206-207) are not part of the lesson body, apart from short question 5, answered in 22.2.2.

items: State the question of the experiment, which defines what you want to find out.
Form a hypothesis: what you expect to happen, based on existing knowledge.
Identify the variables: what you will change (independent), measure (dependent) and keep constant (control).
Set up groups: a control group without the treatment and an experimental group with it.
Plan the procedure in detail: how subjects are chosen and assigned to groups, how each group is treated, the duration and frequency of measurement and how data are collected.
Analyse: use averaging, graphs or statistical tests to compare the groups and judge whether there is a significant effect.
Conclude: relate the results to the hypothesis and the question, and accept or reject the hypothesis.

blocks.text: Worked example: high-fat diet and weight gain in albino mice

items: Question: does a high-fat diet cause greater weight gain in mice than a normal diet?
Hypothesis: mice given a high-fat diet will gain more weight than those on a normal diet.
Variables: independent, type of diet; dependent, weight gain; control, mouse age, strain, sex, cage, environment (light, temperature) and feeding schedule.
Groups: control group on the normal diet; experimental group on the high-fat diet.

Procedure: select albino mice matched by age, strain and sex; assign them randomly to the groups; house all under identical conditions; give each group its diet for a set period, such as 8 weeks; weigh every mouse weekly.
Analysis: compare the average weight gain of the two groups at the end with graphs or statistical tests.

Conclusion: if the high-fat group shows a statistically significant greater average gain, the hypothesis is supported; if there is no significant difference, or the normal-diet group gains more, it is rejected, suggesting other factors matter more under these conditions.
